family: One fixed total language L with slices on all bit lengths N. If N<4 reject. Otherwise choose the largest integer w>=1 with n_w=2*w*2^w<=N, partition the first n_w bits into 2^w consecutive records of 2w bits, and accept iff these records are pairwise distinct; ignore the remaining N-n_w bits. A fixed deterministic polynomial-time pairwise-comparison evaluator decides L. Its NP verifier accepts exactly the empty witness when this evaluator accepts, with witness bound zero.
theorem: For this fixed language L in P, the minimum full-B2 gate count satisfies C_B2(L_N)>=N*log2(log2 N) at every sufficiently large integer input length N, with coefficient one and empty remainder. Consequently for each real A>0 we have C_B2(L_N)>=A*N at every sufficiently large integer N. These are corollaries of Theorem 2.2 of OpenAI, The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths (November 24, 2026), over F_2 on one list. The proof transfers the theorem to unrestricted nonuniform circuits and pads to all lengths while preserving an Omega(N*(log2 N)^sigma) bound for a fixed existential sigma>0.
